subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should OpenAI cache-TTL pruning be enabled through the existing cache-TTL eligibility gate, or should this wait for a retention-aware/provider-agnostic pruning design?
rationale: Source inspection proves the reported gate is real, but enabling it changes session-context behavior for existing OpenAI cache-ttl configs and the linked PR still lacks native idle-gap proof.

options.title: Review the focused OpenAI eligibility PR
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and require the linked PR to add maintainer-approved OpenAI TTL semantics plus redacted native idle-gap proof before merge.

options.title: Replace with provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: Pause the linked one-line eligibility fix and design a pruning mode that does not depend on provider cache-TTL eligibility.

options.title: Document OpenAI as unsupported
options.body: Close only after maintainers explicitly decide configured cache-TTL pruning should remain unsupported for native OpenAI and update docs/diagnostics accordingly.

recommendation.title: Review the focused OpenAI eligibility PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and require the linked PR to add maintainer-approved OpenAI TTL semantics plus redacted native idle-gap proof before merge.
